title: [Shortcut Guide] Taskbar indicators obscure items when taskbar is set to auto-hide
summary: Shortcut Guide positions indicators from the monitor work-area edge, which overlaps a temporarily revealed auto-hidden taskbar.

judgment.rationale: The report is deterministic, and the current layout anchors indicator tails to rcWork rather than the actual taskbar rectangle or auto-hide state.
evidence: The issue supplies current-main reproduction steps and a screenshot.
The taskbar is auto-hidden, then revealed before Shortcut Guide opens.
TaskbarPaneControl anchors indicators a fixed margin inside the work-area edge.
OverlayWindow obtains the monitor work area but does not pass an actual taskbar rectangle or auto-hide state to layout.
judgment.recommended_action: Position the indicator strip from the actual taskbar bounds when a taskbar is present and visible, with work-area fallback only when shell geometry is unavailable.

fix_assessment.rationale: No linked implementation covers auto-hidden taskbar geometry.

proposed_fixes.title: Anchor taskbar indicators outside the live taskbar rectangle
proposed_fixes.root_cause: Indicator layout assumes the work-area edge represents the taskbar boundary. With auto-hide enabled, rcWork can extend to the screen edge while the temporarily shown taskbar overlays that area, so the indicators cover taskbar buttons.
plan: Expose the target monitor's taskbar window rectangle and edge from the native taskbar discovery helper.
Pass the actual taskbar bounds into TaskbarPaneControl.UpdateTasklistButtons.
Place the indicator tail just outside the live taskbar rectangle toward the monitor interior, falling back to work-area placement only when taskbar geometry is unavailable.
Add layout tests for bottom, top, left, and right auto-hidden taskbars.
verification: Enable auto-hide, reveal the taskbar, and invoke Shortcut Guide on every supported taskbar edge.
Confirm indicator bodies do not obscure taskbar icons and tails still point to their buttons.
Verify normal non-auto-hidden taskbar placement and mixed-DPI monitors.

confidence.rationale: The layout calculation explains the overlap, but runtime shell geometry must confirm the correct boundary while auto-hide animation is active.

issue_context.summary: When an auto-hidden taskbar is revealed, Shortcut Guide's numbered indicators are drawn on top of its buttons rather than adjacent to them.
known_information: The report uses current main and includes exact steps and a screenshot.
The taskbar is explicitly revealed before Shortcut Guide activation.
Indicator placement uses the monitor work area and a fixed edge margin.
The layout does not consume the taskbar window rectangle or auto-hide state.
inferences: The monitor work area does not represent the temporarily visible auto-hidden taskbar boundary.
Using live taskbar geometry should handle both auto-hide and non-auto-hide placement consistently.
issue_context.analysis: The current fixed work-area offset is appropriate only when rcWork excludes the taskbar. Auto-hide breaks that assumption, so the layout needs shell taskbar geometry rather than another hard-coded offset.
initial_investigation: Confirmed horizontal and vertical placement are calculated solely from workAreaPhysical and a fixed edge margin.

actions.label: Design auto-hide indicator placement fix
actions.note: Approval starts fork-side design work only; no upstream write occurs automatically.

steps: Move the pointer to the taskbar edge so the taskbar is fully visible.
Invoke Shortcut Guide while the taskbar remains shown.
Repeat for each available taskbar edge and on a secondary monitor.
reproduce.expected_result: Indicator bodies sit adjacent to taskbar buttons without covering them.
reproduce.actual_result_reported: Indicator bodies obscure the taskbar items.

upstream_safety.detail: No public mutation was made to microsoft/PowerToys.
